title: Field Editors and Display Modes: One Field, Many Faces

chapters.title: Field Editors and Display Modes
chapters.subtitle: How a field is entered, and how it is shown

steps.text: A Text Field stores text, but it can appear as a plain box, an email box, a color input, or a set of radio buttons. Editors decide how a value is entered. Display modes decide how it appears on the site.
A content field stores one kind of value. A Text Field stores text, a Numeric Field stores a number, and a Date Field stores a date. Whatever the field looks like, it stores the same kind of value.
The editor is what you see on the edit screen of a content item. A Numeric Field can be a number box, a slider, or a spinner. The editor changes how a value is entered, not what is stored.
The display mode is what visitors see on the site. A Text Field can show its text as it is, or as a heading. You choose the editor and the display mode in the settings of each field.

chapters.title: Choose an editor
chapters.subtitle: A Numeric Field as a slider

steps.text: Design, Content Definition, Content Types lists the content types of the site. Typing Workshop in the Search box narrows the list to that type, and its Edit button opens it.
The Fields list shows the three fields of Workshop, each with its kind next to its name. Seats is a Numeric Field. Its Edit button opens the settings of that field.
The settings of Seats include a Minimum and a Maximum, here zero and forty. Editors such as Slider use them as the two ends of their range.
Below the settings, a drop-down list answers the question What type of editor should be used? Number is selected. Let's choose Slider.
Save returns to the content type. Next to Seats, a badge with the name of the editor, Slider, shows which editor the field uses.
Let's open the New Workshop page. Seats shows a slider track under its number box, running from the minimum, zero, to the maximum, forty.
Dragging the handle changes the number in the box, and typing a number in the box moves the handle. Both set the same value, the number of seats.

chapters.title: An editor with its own settings
chapters.subtitle: A Text Field as a list of choices

steps.text: Some editors bring settings of their own. Skill Level is a Text Field that should hold one of a few levels, so let's open its settings.

Choosing Predefined List in the editor drop-down list reveals the settings of that editor. One asks What type of list editor should be used? Below it, a table holds an Option Label and a Value for each option, here Beginner and Intermediate.
The list editor can be a Drop down list or Radio buttons, and let's pick Radio buttons. Add an option adds a row, and typing the label, Advanced, fills in the value as well.
Each option also has a radio button, under the title Default? Selecting one makes that option the default value. Let's leave them all unselected.
Save stores the options with the field, and the page returns to the content type.
On the New Workshop page, Skill Level is a set of radio buttons, one for each option. Choosing Intermediate selects it.

chapters.title: Choose a display mode
chapters.subtitle: A Text Field as a heading

steps.text: Display modes follow the same pattern. Headline is a Text Field, and its Edit button opens the settings, where the display mode is chosen below the editor.
A drop-down list answers the question What type of display mode should be used? Standard is selected. Let's choose Header.
A setting appears for the display mode: Select the header level to use. Let's choose H2 and Save, and the content type shows a Header badge next to Headline.
On the site, the Headline of the Spring Pottery Evening workshop appears as a second-level heading. A display mode changes only what visitors see; the stored text stays the same.

chapters.title: What each field offers
chapters.subtitle: Editors and display modes of the Content Fields module

steps.text: Each field offers its own editors. A Text Field offers Standard, Code Mirror, Color, Email, Icon picker, Monaco editor, Multi-line, Phone, Predefined List and Url. A Numeric Field offers Number, Range, Select, Slider and Spinner.

A Boolean Field offers Standard and Switch, and a Multi Text Field offers Standard, Checkbox List and Picker. A Date Field offers Standard and Localized. The Date Time Field and the Time Field offer Standard only.
Display modes are less common. A Text Field offers Standard and Header, and a User Picker Field offers Standard and User Names. Every other field of the Content Fields module offers Standard only.
One field can serve many purposes: the editor shapes the edit screen, the display mode shapes the site, and the stored value stays the same. Thanks for watching.
